note: Forest Service campground in maple, aspen and white pine along the north shore of 86-acre Lost Lake (no motors of any kind), with a sandy swim beach, a boat access and trails to a 150-year-old hemlock-pine stand and on to Chipmunk Rapids and the Lauterman Trail. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov facility/rates/catalog read. 27 nonelectric back-in sites (30-40 ft), $15, vault toilets, water; 14 reservable in peak season; season 04-30..10-13 (manual, matches). Lakeview kept: the lake-side row (3-24) is ~50-60 m from the shore under continuous canopy; the FS page's 'waterfront sites' and rec.gov 'Lakefront' tags are a contrary-claim lead. Closed for the season now (normal).
flags: WATERFRONT: stored lakeview kept, but a contrary claim to re-audit upward. The FS page says 'Take advantage of our waterfront sites on the shore of the crystal-clear Lost Lake' and rec.gov tags 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23 and 24 'Lakefront'. On Esri imagery the whole campground is under continuous maple/aspen canopy; the lake-side row sits ~50-60 m from the shoreline (site 4 45.88298,-88.56190 ~57 m; 8 45.88302,-88.56121 ~54 m; 15 45.88315,-88.55880 ~50 m; 20 45.88301,-88.55721 ~60 m; 22-24 ~90-100 m by the catalog points). The rec.gov photos (spring, leaf-off) of sites 8 and 9 show the lake ~25-40 m beyond the pad across open forest floor through trunks; 15, 18 and 20 show it farther through trees. Under the canopy rule this is a view. If the reviewer accepts the open forest floor, sites 8 (reservable) and 9 (reservable, 30 ft) are the candidates for lakefront-with-caveat. All sites are sold by the night.
